title: Mongoose setup
idea: Mongoose is a library that gives MongoDB documents a shape in your app: a schema describes the fields, and a model reads and writes one collection.
points: `mongoose.connect(uri)` opens the default connection; call it once, at startup.
A schema lists each field's type and rules, such as `required` and `trim`.
`mongoose.model('Book', schema)` returns a model bound to the `books` collection.
Mongoose casts values to the schema's types, then validates, before any insert.

hero.title: A book on its way to MongoDB

steps.caption: `Book.create` gets a plain object. The title has spaces and `year` is the string `'1965'`.
Cast turns `'1965'` into the number `1965`. `trim` strips the spaces from the title.
Validation checks the cast values: `title`, `author` and `year` are all present.
Only now does Mongoose send the insert. The stored document also gets `_id` and `__v`, a version counter.
A second book has no `author`, and its `year` is the string `'soon'`.
`'soon'` cannot become a number. Mongoose records a `CastError` for `year` and carries on.
`author` is missing, so `required` fails. Both problems end up in one `ValidationError`.
`create` rejects with that error. The insert never happens, so MongoDB stores nothing.

code.title: Schema, model, validation
code.caption: One schema and one model. Step through it, then press Run for the real output.

walk.text: The schema sets each field's type and rules. `Book` is the model for the `books` collection.
Connect once. Here `MONGO_URI` points at a local MongoDB.
`create` casts `'1965'` to a number and trims the title before saving.
This book has no author and a `year` that is not a number, so `create` rejects.
`err.errors` has one entry per bad field: a `CastError` for `year`, a `ValidatorError` for `author`.
Only the first book was stored. `select` hides `_id` and `__v`; `lean()` returns plain objects.
Disconnect so the script can exit.

pitfalls: Fields missing from the schema are dropped silently: a typo such as `Year` is never saved.
Query updates such as `findByIdAndUpdate` skip validators unless you pass `runValidators: true`.
A schema guards only your app; other clients can still write any shape.

quiz.why: Mongoose trims the title and casts `'1815'` to a number. `mood` is not in the schema, so it is dropped.

takeaway: Before `create` or `save` writes, Mongoose casts and checks against the schema.

starters: Do I have to define a schema in Mongoose?
Why did Mongoose name my collection `books`?
